assign.outcome:
**core/Layout landed — thirty arrangements you can browse, every one proven at seven widths.**

![](tree-3440.png)

[**The tree**](/framework/core/Layout/) is a wall of small pictures under one sentence, One column first. A rail filters it — columns, tags, approved/draft, band — and every filter starts at *everything*, so the first thing you see is the whole set. Sixty cards draw, then a *show more*.

[**A layout page**](/framework/core/Layout/main-aside/) opens the layout at its own narrowest proven width with a handle to drag, the seven-width strip beside it (a pane below the floor draws the fallback and says so), the props a filter reads, and two walls — variations and alternatives.

**Thirty, and not one invented**: 18 from `/imagine/layouts/system.js`, 11 from `ext/DesignTool/library/patterns.js`, 1 from `styles/layouts/masonry`. Every entry keeps its source's prose.

**Thirty approved, zero drafts** — after the fixtures found four on the first pass and each one was a real defect in the port, now fixed. One ragged finding stands: `toolbar-cluster` at 400px, which is a control row, where raggedness is the point.

**The rules are three**: a width range, contrast, and nesting that breaks a mechanism — everything else on the list turned out to be something CSS already answers. Dev only, a dashed outline and a badge, never a block.
